clue.text: The picture's about the staging of a play

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning
putting a play on stage is mounting a production

explanation.surface: A painting depicts a theatre company putting on a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy of an artwork, such as a print of a famous painting, is a picture in its own right.

clue.text: Creating a safety measure

explanation.surface: A note about devising a precaution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creating' here is British slang for kicking up a fuss, complaining loudly, which is what railing means.
explanation.definitionFit: Railing means ranting or protesting angrily (British 'creating'), and a railing is a protective barrier fence.

clue.text: Lodger dashed inside and — crash!

indicators.note: the word for dashed goes inside the letters for lodger

parts.note: PG is a paying guest, a lodger
ran means hurried or dashed

explanation.surface: A lodger rushes indoors and there is a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a crash, especially a car or plane collision.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is informal British for a crash or collision, usually of a vehicle.

clue.text: Clothier striking tailor's assistant .

parts.note: workers out on strike are said to be out
a fitter adjusts garments to fit, working for a tailor

explanation.surface: A clothes shop's assistant goes on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter sells clothing, especially men's wear or uniforms.

clue.text: Accustomed to being exploited

explanation.surface: Someone has grown resigned to being taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: Used to means habituated, and to be used is to be taken advantage of.

clue.text: Terrier's disorder in an Australian state

parts.note: a Terrier is a member of the Territorial Army, TA, so a Terrier's gives TAS
a mania is a mental disorder or obsession

explanation.surface: A small dog's obsession is found in a part of Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrier' wants to be the dog; in British slang it is a Territorial Army volunteer, giving TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is the island state of Australia, south of the mainland.

clue.text: Sovereign invested by pensioner on one animal

indicators.note: to be invested is to be clothed or surrounded, so the sovereign goes inside the pensioner

parts.note: OAP is an old-age pensioner
K stands for king, a sovereign
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pensioner puts a gold coin into one creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign' suggests the gold coin, but it is the king. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a giraffe relative from the Congo rainforest, a striped mammal.

clue.text: Halma is played on bar in mess in Moorish citadel

indicators.note: the letters of Halma and bar are in a mess, rearranged

explanation.surface: A board game is played on a bar counter in an army mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Halma is a board game; 'mess' looks like a military dining room but signals rearranging HALMA and BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the Moorish palace-fortress at Granada in Spain.

clue.text: Stick to this time and place

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era
here means in this place

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay put at this moment and spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or stay attached, as glue does.

clue.text: Unsuitability in a couple of points

parts.note: taken as written
PT is the abbreviation for point, and a ness is a point of land, a headland
a ness is a headland or promontory, a point jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Something is judged unsuitable on a couple of counts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple of points' gives two different points: PT, the short form, and NESS, a headland (as in Loch Ness's neighbour Orford Ness).
explanation.definitionFit: Being inapt means being ill-fitted to the purpose, hence the quality of being wrong for something.

clue.text: Cried after wife disappeared, and became ill

indicators.note: the wife has vanished from the word for crying, so her letter is taken out

parts.note: to wail is to cry loudly in grief

explanation.surface: Someone wept after their wife vanished and then fell sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailed is the past tense of ail, to be unwell or suffer illness.

clue.text: Girl shows where the power is

explanation.surface: A young woman reveals the location of the authority.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the girl's name as IN GRID: electrical power is in the national grid, the network that carries it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a female forename; and electricity is carried in the grid, the supply network of cables.

clue.text: Mockery is unpleasant in the latter part of life

parts.note: something bad is nasty or unpleasant
taken as written
age, as in old age, is the late stage of a life

explanation.surface: Ridicule turns nasty as one gets older.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful teasing or banter, a light kind of mocking talk.

clue.text: Go initially to the awful slum area

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word Go is wanted here
the words to the are made into an awful jumble, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to head first to a dreadful run-down district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges TO THE into HETTO, placed after G.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a deprived, overcrowded quarter of a city, often a poor run-down neighbourhood.

clue.text: One mug for a German physicist

parts.note: ein is German for one, prompted by the German in the clue
a stein is a large beer mug

explanation.surface: A single tankard for a German scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein, born in Ulm, devised the theory of relativity.

clue.text: Liberal President, competent and attractive

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics
Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight D. Eisenhower
able means capable or competent

explanation.surface: A description of an appealing politician: liberal, presidential, capable and attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone likeable is pleasant and easy to warm to, so appealing.

clue.text: Forty of the Romans are said to '. have advanced — splendid!

indicators.note: the Roman letters are spoken, which sounds like a word for doing well

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals
lent means advanced, as money is advanced on loan

explanation.surface: Forty Roman soldiers are reported to have pushed forward, gloriously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are said to' signals that XL is read out as 'ex-ell'; 'advanced' means loaned, not moved forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent is an exclamation of approval meaning superb.

clue.text: Criminals in gang get it either way

parts.note: a band is a group or gang
taken as written

indicators.note: the word it is taken both forwards and backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gangsters in a mob will cop it whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'either way' gives IT forwards and backwards, IT then TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditti is the Italian-style plural of bandit, a band of outlaws or robbers.

clue.text: It's unnatural to ban moral reform

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters of ban moral are reshaped

explanation.surface: A view that banning moral reform goes against nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' looks like the object of 'ban', but it is the anagram signal working on BAN MORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormal means deviating from what is usual or natural.

clue.text: Athletic woman, needed for the river

explanation.surface: A sporty woman is wanted at the riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: An amazon is a tall strong woman, after the mythical warrior women; the Amazon is the great South American river.

clue.text: Circular letter about tax return — nothing in book form

parts.note: O is the round letter of the alphabet
C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: the tax word is returned, so it is read backwards

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A circular about a tax return says nothing in written form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax return' poses as the form you send in; here 'return' only turns the tax round.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavo is a book size in which each printed sheet is folded into eight leaves.

clue.text: Agreed with boy to have no mount for long journey

indicators.note: in a down clue, to mount is to climb, so the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: yes is a word of agreement
Syd is a boy's name, short for Sydney
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A parent agrees to a boy's trip without a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' looks like a horse; it signals reading YES, SYD and O upwards in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An odyssey is any long eventful journey, after Odysseus's ten-year voyage home.

clue.text: A pointed exchange of letters? Just the opposite

indicators.note: the letters of the words A pointed swap places with one another, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A sharp correspondence between two people turns out to be the reverse of friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange of letters' reads as correspondence by post but means the letters of A POINTED are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An antipode is the direct opposite of something, literally the point on the far side of the globe.

clue.text: Infectious fright of an immortal

explanation.surface: Terror spreads from a god.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the word as Pan-ic, an adjective meaning of the god Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden contagious alarm, named after the god Pan, and as an adjective panic means relating to Pan.

clue.text: Magazine showing good life on yacht starts outside the vessel

parts.note: L is a recognised abbreviation for life

indicators.note: the two opening letters sit outside, on either side of, the vessel
only the opening letters of the words on and yacht are used

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A glamorous magazine shows the good life on board a yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes O and Y from 'on yacht'; 'outside' puts them either side of SS.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy is a magazine printed on shiny paper, typically about fashion and celebrity.

clue.text: Time to arrange the letters

explanation.surface: A note on the time needed to sort letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a period, and to spell is to give the letters of a word in order.

clue.text: Man I'll sound like

indicators.note: the clue says the abbreviation of I will is to be heard as a word

parts.note: these words are said aloud, and what is heard is the sound this part of the answer needs

explanation.surface: A man promises he will sound similar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person; it is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Man, in the Irish Sea, is an island, hence an example of the place word.

clue.text: One of the plants well known to an expert

definitions.text: One of the plants well known to an expert

parts.words: One of the plants well known to an expert
parts.note: plays on the British idiom that an expert 'knows their' bulbous vegetables, meaning knows the subject thoroughly

explanation.surface: A botanist names a plant a specialist would recognise.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English someone who knows their onions is an expert, so this vegetable is the one an expert proverbially knows.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'to know your onions' means to be expert, so this plant is literally well known to experts.

clue.text: Dont try so hard to be undiscriminating

explanation.surface: Advice to ease off if one wants to be less choosy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first definition as TASTE LESS: to taste is to try, so 'try less hard'.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste less means sample less (try less hard), and tasteless means lacking discernment or refinement.

clue.text: Can dice turn out to be the same by chance?

indicators.note: the letters of can dice are turned out into a new arrangement

parts.note: two accounts tally when they agree, are the same

explanation.surface: A gambler wonders whether dice can come up identical by luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out' rearranges CAN DICE to ACCIDEN; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Accidentally means happening by luck or fortune, without design.
